'''Dennis Horner''' (born February 5, 1988) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Instituto de Córdoba]] of the Argentine [[Liga Nacional de Básquet]].

==Early life and college==
Horner grew up in [[Linwood, New Jersey]], and attended [[Holy Spirit High School (New Jersey)|Holy Spirit High School]] in [[Absecon, New Jersey]], where he was named the co-basketball player of the year in 2006 by ''[[The Press of Atlantic City]]''.<ref>[http://www.pressofatlanticcity.com/communities/northfield_linwood_somers-point/holy-spirit-graduate-dennis-horner-makes-the-new-jersey-nets/article_5443abc8-2da7-11e1-8fd1-001871e3ce6c.html Holy Spirit graduate Dennis Horner makes the New Jersey Nets regular-season roster] by SUSAN LULGJURAJ, staff writer, press of Atlantic City. Saturday, December 24, 2011</ref> He is an alumnus of the [[North Carolina State University]] [[North Carolina State Wolfpack basketball|men's basketball team]]. In his final season (2009–10), Horner averaged 11.9 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.<ref>[http://northcarolina.rivals.com/bviewplayer.asp?Player=65132 player page at rivals.com]</ref>

==Professional==
After college, Horner started the 2010–11 season with [[RBC Verviers-Pepinster]] but after not appearing in a game for them, he signed a contract in Cyprus for club [[Omonia BC]] where he played 13 games averaging 11.6 points in 29.3 minutes. Before the 2011–12 season, he made himself eligible for the [[NBA Development League]] draft, where he was picked 47th overall by the [[Springfield Armor]], which was in the process of becoming affiliated solely with the NBA's [[New Jersey Nets]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2011/index.html 2011 NBA D-League Draft Results] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111207031237/http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2011/index.html |date=December 7, 2011 }}</ref> In December, it was announced Horner was one of three players on the Armor invited to Nets' training camp following the [[2011 NBA lockout]]. At that point he had been averaging 15.0 points, 7.7 rebounds and 1.2 assists for Springfield.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/armor_players_invited__nba_t_2011_12_20.html Armor Players Invited to NBA Training Camps] NBA D-League website</ref> On December 23, the Nets announced that Horner had made the team, and would start the season on the Nets' roster.<ref>[http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2011/12/nets_finalize_roster_by_waivin.html Nets finalize roster by waiving Ime Udoka, keeping Linwood native Dennis Horner] By Jorge Castillo, The Star-Ledger of Newark, December 23, 2011</ref> Horner was waived by the Nets on January 18, 2012.<ref>[http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2012/01/nets_send_jordan_williams_to_d.html Nets send Jordan Williams to D-League; waive Dennis Horner, sign Larry Owens]</ref> Horner then returned to the Springfield Armor.

On March 30, 2012, Horner was re-signed by the Nets on a 10-day contract.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets_sign_dennis_horner_to_10_day_contract_120330.html NETS Sign Dennis Horner to 10-Day Contract]</ref>

In October 2012, he signed with the [[Artland Dragons]] of Germany.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2012-13/i/100889/7363/artland-dragons-inks-horner-at-forward |title=ARTLAND DRAGONS inks Horner at forward |access-date=2014-08-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808055911/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2012-13/i/100889/7363/artland-dragons-inks-horner-at-forward |archive-date=2014-08-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He left in November 2012.

On January 3, 2013, Horner was re-acquired by the [[Springfield Armor]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/armor_reacquire_dennis_horner_2013_01_03.html Armor Re-acquire Dennis Horner]</ref> On November 1, 2013, he was re-acquired by the Armor for their 2013 training camp.<ref>{{cite web|title=Returning Players Highlight Initial Training Camp Invites |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/returning_players_for_2013201_2013_11_01.html |work=NBA.com |date=November 1, 2013 |accessdate=November 1, 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204005917/http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/returning_players_for_2013201_2013_11_01.html |archivedate=December 4, 2013 }}</ref> On February 20, 2014, he was traded to the Bakersfield Jam.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_trade_armor_jam_legends_2014_02_20.html Five Former NBA Players Traded in Three-Team Deal] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301184717/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_trade_armor_jam_legends_2014_02_20.html |date=2014-03-01 }}</ref>

On August 1, 2014, he signed a one-year deal with Artland Dragons, returning for second stint.<ref>{{cite news|title=Artland Dragons brings back Horner|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/139951|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808055924/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/139951|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 8, 2014|accessdate=August 1, 2014|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=August 1, 2014}}</ref>
